description.value: The study evaluated whether early 11C-PIB PET perfusion frames provide information comparable to 18F-FDG PET metabolism for differentiating Alzheimer’s disease from frontotemporal lobar degeneration.

spans.text: In this study we investigated whether early 11C-PIB PET frames (perfusion, pPIB) can provide information equivalent to blood flow and metabolism by assessing the similarity of pPIB and 18F-FDG PET images first in a test cohort with various clinical diagnoses (N=10) and then validating the results on a cohort of Alzheimer’s disease (AD, N=42, age 66.6±10.6, MMSE 22.2±6.0) and frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD, N=31, age 63.9±7.1, MMSE 23.8±6.7) patients.

description.value: A test cohort was used to identify the optimal pPIB timeframe, which was then validated in an extended cohort of Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal lobar degeneration patients.

spans.text: We used a small testing cohort of subjects with a variety of dementias to determine the optimal timeframe representing perfusion from the PIB data. This timeframe was then validated on a larger cohort of AD and FTLD patients.
Two cohorts were used in this study: the test cohort (N=10) and the validation cohort (N=73).

definition.value: For every 0.01 increase in the tracer value in the temporal pole, a subject has higher odds of being diagnosed as AD as opposed to FTLD.

spans.text: There were six PIB positive and 4 PIB negative subjects, as determined by visual interpretation.

value: The temporal pole was a significant discriminator in the pPIB model (P < 0.05). For every 0.01 unit increase in the pPIB value in the temporal pole, a subject had higher odds of being diagnosed with AD as opposed to FTLD.

definition.value: For every incremental increase in the pPIB value in the temporal neocortex region, a subject has lower odds of being diagnosed as AD as opposed to FTLD.

value: The temporal neocortex was a significant discriminator in the pPIB model (P < 0.05). For every incremental increase of the pPIB value in the temporal neocortex region, a subject had lower odds of being diagnosed as AD, which is expected since this region is more hypometabolic in AD than FTLD.

value: The temporal pole was a significant discriminator in the 18F-FDG model (P < 0.05). The temporal pole and temporal neocortex shared directionality and acted similarly in discriminating AD from FTLD.

definition.value: The temporal neocortex was a significant discriminator in the 18F-FDG model.

value: The temporal neocortex was a significant discriminator in the 18F-FDG model (P < 0.05). For every incremental increase of the 18F-FDG value in the temporal neocortex region, a subject had lower odds of being diagnosed as AD, which is expected since this region is more hypometabolic in AD than FTLD.
